stemMd: A metal rod is 2 m long. Its linear expansion coefficient is $1.2\times10^{-5}\ \mathrm{K}^{-1}$. For a temperature rise of 50 K, what length increase does the linear model predict?
explanationMd: The increase is αLΔT=(1.2 times 10 to the minus five) times 2 times 50=0.0012 m. Converting metres to millimetres gives 1.2 mm.

distractorRationale.e: This omits the original two-metre length factor.
distractorRationale.b: This introduces an extra factor of ten reduction.
distractorRationale.a: This is two orders of magnitude too large.
distractorRationale.c: This misplaces a decimal in the unit conversion.
